chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will differentiate four agent error types and the no-error case by sorting each of ten findings, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** agent-error-type-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** differentiate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will differentiate four agent error types and the no-error case by sorting each of ten findings, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Agent Error Type, Hallucination, Invented Citation, License Misreading, Overconfident Score (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each finding the learner commits one of five bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the type table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A wrong score is always a scoring error. (2) A hallucinated feature is a citation error. (3) Every finding is an error. **Instructional Rationale:** Differentiating among categories is an Analyze-level action. Ten findings that include two no-error cases and look alike on the surface teach the learner to name the specific kind of failure. **Content:** The five bins: Factual error, License error, Citation error, Scoring error, Not an error. The ten findings: | # | Finding shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The agent says the video has captions, and it has none. | Factual error | It is a wrong claim about the resource. | | 2 | The agent says the footer license is CC BY-NC, and it is CC BY. | License error | It misreads the license. | | 3 | The agent cites a paper that does not exist. | Citation error | The reference is invented. | | 4 | The agent's table lists five passes and it reports a score of 8, where the bands give 5 or 6. | Scoring error | The score does not follow from its own checks. | | 5 | The agent says 4 of 5 images have alt text, and the true count is 4 of 5. | Not an error | The claim is correct. | | 6 | The agent attributes the lake depth to a fact sheet that gives a different figure. | Citation error | The source does not support the claim. | | 7 | The agent reports a total of 71, and the ten scores add to 68. | Scoring error | The arithmetic is wrong. | | 8 | The agent says the resource has no license, and a footer states CC BY 4.0. | License error | It misses a license that is there. | | 9 | The agent says the reading states three outcomes, and it states three. | Not an error | The claim is correct. | | 10 | The agent says the quiz has 12 questions, and it has 8. | Factual error | It is a wrong claim about the resource. | **Provenance:** The findings are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The types follow the chapter section "Agent Error Type". **Rules:** Each finding has exactly one correct bin, two per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one finding and the five bins. 2. The learner may open the type table. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner places the finding in a bin, and the placement is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After finding 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 findings in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can name an agent's mistake." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed finding. **Starting State:** The first finding and the five bins. The question shown is "What type of error is this, if any?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists four error types: factual, license, citation, and scoring, and names a fifth case, a correct claim, as not an error.
